reaction: Called Murmur but page says Two Voices. Third week? I have not played a first. I leave boxes empty and press Start.

input.name: Get up and put your feet on the floor. She would agree only if you insist. Hold to insist. This costs trust.

reaction: A 55 second clock. I am a dispatcher, people get up at the alarm. I hold to insist.

input.name: Tell Aylin you will call Mum tonight on the bus. She would agree only if you insist.

reaction: Lines repeat twice on the screen, a little messy. Insist again, a promise to the sister is sensible. I worry about spending trust I cannot see.

input.name: Talk her through it. She would agree only if you insist.

reaction: This is my job, a lost driver on the radio. You talk them through. Insisting a third time, I hope trust lasts.

I understand it: little scenes, I push her one way, the other voice in pencil pushes the other. Clear enough. The countdown bothers me a bit, but skip ahead is welcome. Screen keeps growing and lines appear twice.

input.name: “She found it, didn’t she?” She would agree only if you insist.

reaction: A supervisor mocking a new driver. Not in my control room. She should say it.

input.name: Have the coffee. She is willing.

reaction: I have insisted four times; I do not know how much trust is left, there is no number. I let her have the coffee. Shift workers know.

input.name: Call Mum. She wants to do it later.

reaction: She promised Aylin. I want her to keep it. No hold hint here, so I just click. Guessing what wants to do it later means.

She refused me and scrolled. Fair, I could not insist on that one, there was no hold offered. But the promise to Aylin is broken and nobody tells me why I could not push. I would like to see the trust I have left.
Missed her stop by two. As a transit person I smile. Consequence is clear, I like that.

input.name: Put the phone on the floor and go to sleep. She wants to do it later.

reaction: I try holding even without the hint, maybe it works like insist.
"You keep pushing me." So trust ran out. Now I understand: insisting is a budget, and I spent it in the morning. That is a clear cause, I accept it, but I wish I had seen a counter.

error: Skip to the next event is not on the page now; it was listed 3 s ago and the page has changed; copy one full name from clickable in this reply (game state, not a driver failure)

reaction: This end-of-day page is what I wanted: a tick, a crossed-out call, her opinion of me. Like a shift report. Good. Tuesday, I will push less.
The third coffee comes back. Cause and effect, I like it, a bit guilty.
I stay quiet to give her trust back. I hope silence is the way to repair it; I am guessing.

input.name: Say you overslept. She wants to do it later.

reaction: "She wants to do it later" for telling the truth? The wording does not fit; it means no, I think. I click honesty anyway. Oh, I silenced her and she slept through three alarms. Lesson.

input.name: “That was me.” She wants to do it later.

reaction: A routing mistake. In my job you own it. I hold to insist; I said nothing this morning so maybe trust is back.
The people and the work feel real to me, a depot, a routing error. But now she refuses everything I want and I cannot see why trust did not come back overnight. I am losing my grip on the rule.

The i page explains it: trust shows in how dark my handwriting is. I would never have read that from the letters. A number would be kinder. And blaming the system pointed at Ece, poor girl. That stings.

input.name: Ask Ece where she takes a break away from the depot. She wants to do it later.

reaction: I only suggest, no pushing. A small kindness toward Ece after the scanner.

reaction: "They think it was Ece." That is the line that hurts, and it is my doing too. The summary is good. But Tuesday was the same shape as Monday and she refused me four times. I do not want four more days of this tonight.

I stop at Tuesday night. I liked the depot and Ece, and the bedtime summary. But I spent her trust on Monday morning without knowing it was a budget, and since then she refuses me. Two days the same shape. Enough for tonight.
